1094.idea: Add passengers at each pickup and subtract at each drop-off in a difference array, then sweep the stops and check the running load never exceeds capacity.
1094.pitfall: Subtracting at to + 1, when riders leave at to and free their seats there.
1094.time: O(n + L), n = trips, L = max stop

1110.title: Delete Nodes And Return Forest
1110.idea: Work post-order, since a kept node becomes a new root when it has no kept parent, and a deleted node hands null back to its parent.
1110.pitfall: Not clearing the parent's link to a deleted child.

1143.title: Longest Common Subsequence
1143.idea: If the last characters match, extend the diagonal by one, otherwise take the better of dropping a last character from either string.
1143.pitfall: With a rolling row, overwriting the diagonal value before reading it; save it in a temporary.

1146.title: Snapshot Array
1146.idea: Each index keeps its own sorted list of (snap id, value) changes, so get binary searches for the last change at or before the snapshot.
1146.pitfall: Copying the whole array on snap, which costs O(n) per call and exhausts memory.
1146.time: O(1) per set and snap, O(log S) per get, S = changes at that index

1218.title: Longest Arithmetic Subsequence of Given Difference
1218.idea: The best chain ending at v is 1 plus the best ending at v - difference, stored in a hash map.
1218.pitfall: Using the O(n^2) pairwise DP, which times out.

1235.title: Maximum Profit in Job Scheduling
1235.idea: Sort by start, and dp[i] is the best of skipping to job i + 1 or taking job i plus dp at the first job starting at or after its end, found by binary search.
1235.pitfall: Searching for a start strictly after the end, when a job may begin exactly as the last one ends.

1254.title: Number of Closed Islands
1254.idea: First erase all land connected to the border, then each remaining component is closed.
1254.pitfall: Using short-circuit && across recursive calls, which stops before visiting the whole island.

1277.title: Count Square Submatrices with All Ones
1277.idea: The largest square ending at a cell equals the number of squares ending there, so sum all dp values.
1277.pitfall: Summing only the inner cells, which drops 1 x 1 squares in the first row and column.

1293.title: Shortest Path in a Grid with Obstacles Elimination
1293.idea: BFS over states (row, col, removals left), since all steps cost 1, and at each cell keep only the largest removals-left seen, because arriving later with fewer can't help.
1293.pitfall: Tracking visited by cell alone, which rejects a later arrival that has more removals left.

1353.title: Maximum Number of Events That Can Be Attended
1353.idea: Walk days in order, add events starting today to a min-heap of end days, and attend the one ending soonest.
1353.pitfall: Not popping events whose end day has passed.
1353.time: O(n log n + D), D = last event day

1406.title: Stone Game III
1406.idea: dp[i] is the best lead for the player to move at i, found by taking 1 to 3 stones and subtracting dp at the new position.
1406.pitfall: Seeding the max with 0, when all-negative stones still force a take.

1438.title: Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Diff Less Than or Equal to Limit
1438.idea: Two monotonic deques give the window's max and min in O(1), so shrink left while max - min exceeds the limit.
1438.pitfall: Not popping deque fronts when left moves past those indices.

1482.title: Minimum Number of Days to Make m Bouquets
1482.idea: Feasibility only improves with more days, so binary search the day, counting runs of k bloomed flowers.
1482.pitfall: Not returning -1 when m * k > n, a product that can overflow int.
1482.time: O(n log D), D = max bloom day

1526.title: Minimum Number of Increments on Subarrays to Form a Target Array
1526.idea: Only rises need new operations, since a drop is covered by ranges already open, so the answer is target[0] plus all positive steps.
1526.pitfall: Simulating the range increments, which is quadratic.

1539.title: Kth Missing Positive Number
1539.idea: arr[i] - i - 1 counts positives missing before arr[i] and never decreases, so find the first index lo with at least k missing, and the answer is lo + k.
1539.pitfall: Building the answer from an array value, which fails when the kth missing number lies before arr[0].

1631.title: Path With Minimum Effort
1631.idea: Run Dijkstra where a path's cost is its largest step, not a sum, relaxing neighbors with max(current, step).
1631.pitfall: Adding the edge weight as in normal Dijkstra instead of taking the max.

1658.title: Minimum Operations to Reduce X to Zero
1658.idea: Removing from the ends leaves a middle block, so find the longest subarray summing to total - x.
1658.pitfall: Not handling total - x = 0, where the whole array is removed.

1769.title: Minimum Number of Operations to Move All Balls to Each Box
1769.idea: Sweep left then right, since each box's cost from one side is the previous cost plus the balls seen so far.
1769.pitfall: Updating the ball count before the cost in a sweep, which charges a ball for reaching its own box.

1825.title: Finding MK Average
1825.idea: Keep the last m values in a queue plus three ordered multisets (k smallest, middle, k largest) and a running sum of the middle.
1825.pitfall: Not rebalancing the three sets after both the insertion and the removal.
1825.time: O(log m) per add, O(1) per calculate

1834.title: Single-Threaded CPU
1834.idea: Sort tasks by enqueue time and keep available ones in a min-heap by (processing time, index), and when the heap is empty, jump the clock to the next enqueue time.
1834.pitfall: Stepping the clock by 1 through idle gaps, which is too slow.

1838.title: Frequency of the Most Frequent Element
1838.idea: After sorting, the best target is a window's right end, and the cost is value * size minus window sum, which must stay within k.
1838.pitfall: Computing the cost in int, which overflows.

1922.title: Count Good Numbers
1922.idea: Even positions have 5 choices and odd positions 4, so the count is 5^ceil(n/2) * 4^floor(n/2) modulo 1e9 + 7, using fast exponentiation.
1922.pitfall: Looping over n, which can reach 1e15.

1944.title: Number of Visible People in a Queue
1944.idea: Scan right to left with a stack of decreasing heights, since a person sees each shorter person they pop, plus one more if the stack is still non-empty.
1944.pitfall: Forgetting that extra +1 for the taller person left on the stack.

2034.title: Stock Price Fluctuation
2034.idea: Keep a timestamp-to-price map for corrections and a multiset of live prices for max and min, removing the old price on an update.
2034.pitfall: Calling multiset::erase with a value, which deletes all equal prices; erase the iterator from find.

2035.title: Partition Array Into Two Arrays to Minimize Sum Difference
2035.idea: Meet in the middle: list subset sums of each half by pick count, then for a picks on the left, binary search among n - a picks on the right for the sum closest to half the total.
2035.pitfall: Mixing pick counts, when a picks on the left must pair with exactly n - a on the right.
2035.time: O(n 2^n), n = half the array length

2096.title: Step-By-Step Directions From a Binary Tree Node to Another
2096.idea: Find root-to-start and root-to-dest paths as letter strings, strip the common prefix, which reaches the LCA, then turn what remains of the start path into U moves.
2096.pitfall: Copying a path string into every recursive call, which uses O(n^2) memory on a skewed tree.

2101.title: Detonate the Maximum Bombs
2101.idea: Bomb i reaching bomb j is a directed edge since radii differ, so DFS from each bomb and take the largest reach.
2101.pitfall: Treating edges as undirected, for example with union-find.

2115.title: Find All Possible Recipes from Given Supplies
2115.idea: Point each ingredient at the recipes that need it and run Kahn's from the supplies, so a recipe becomes ready when its count of missing ingredients reaches zero, and then it acts as a supply.
2115.pitfall: Using a plain recursive check with no cycle guard, which loops on recipes that depend on each other.
2115.time: O(R + I + S), R = recipes, I = total ingredient entries, S = supplies

2149.title: Rearrange Array Elements by Sign
2149.idea: Write positives to even indices and negatives to odd indices of a new array, each with its own pointer, which keeps relative order.
2149.pitfall: Trying to swap in place, which breaks the relative order.

2188.title: Minimum Time to Finish the Race
2188.idea: Precompute best[k], the fastest k straight laps on one tire, which stops paying off after about 18 laps, then dp[i] = min over k of dp[i - k] + best[k] + changeTime.
2188.pitfall: Not capping streak length, so lap times overflow.
2188.time: O((T + L) K), T = tires, L = laps, K = about 18

2203.title: Minimum Weighted Subgraph With the Required Paths
2203.idea: The two paths merge at some node and share the rest, so run Dijkstra from src1, from src2, and from dest on the reversed graph, then minimize the three distances' sum over all nodes.
2203.pitfall: Running the third Dijkstra on the forward graph, when distances to dest need reversed edges.

2226.title: Maximum Candies Allocated to K Children
2226.idea: If every child can get c candies, any smaller c also works, so binary search c while the sum of pile / c >= k.
2226.pitfall: Starting the search at c = 0, which divides by zero; search from 1 and treat 0 as the fallback answer.
2226.time: O(n log M), M = max pile

2332.title: The Latest Time to Catch a Bus
2332.idea: Sort both arrays and simulate boarding, then the candidate is the last bus's departure if a seat remains, else just before its last boarded passenger, stepping back past taken times.
2332.pitfall: Forgetting that the candidate can't equal another passenger's arrival time.
2332.time: O(n log n + m log m), n = buses, m = passengers

2333.title: Minimum Sum of Squared Difference
2333.idea: Only |a - b| matters and the two budgets pool into k = k1 + k2, so always lower the largest differences, leveling them down together.
2333.pitfall: Spending one unit at a time on a heap, which is far too slow for a budget near 2e9.

2337.title: Move Pieces to Obtain a String
2337.idea: Pieces can't cross, so the L and R sequences without blanks must be equal, and then each L may only move left and each R only right.
2337.pitfall: Comparing only the piece sequences and ignoring the direction limits on positions.

2349.title: Design a Number Container System
2349.idea: Keep index-to-number plus, for each number, an ordered set of indices, erasing an index from its old number on change.
2349.pitfall: With lazy min-heaps, not checking that a popped index still holds that number.
2349.time: O(log n) per operation, n = change calls

2402.title: Meeting Rooms III
2402.idea: Hold free rooms in a min-heap by number and busy rooms in one by (end time, number), and when no room is free, delay the meeting to the earliest end time, keeping its duration.
2402.pitfall: Using int for end times, which delays can push past 32 bits.
2402.time: O(m log m + m log n), m = meetings, n = rooms

2663.title: Lexicographically Smallest Beautiful String
2663.idea: Avoiding palindromes of length 2 and 3 avoids all longer ones, so bump the rightmost position that can rise validly, then fill the suffix with the smallest legal letters.
2663.pitfall: Not resetting the suffix to its smallest legal letters after the bump.

2762.title: Continuous Subarrays
2762.idea: Two monotonic deques track the window's max and min, shrink left while their gap exceeds 2, and each right end adds right - left + 1 subarrays.
2762.pitfall: Counting in int, when the total can reach about n^2 / 2.

2812.title: Find the Safest Path in a Grid
2812.idea: Multi-source BFS from all thieves gives each cell's safeness, then a max-heap Dijkstra maximizes the path's minimum.
2812.pitfall: Running a BFS from each thief separately, which is too slow.

3026.title: Maximum Good Subarray Sum
3026.idea: For an end value v the start must be v - k or v + k, so store each value's minimum prefix sum before it and query both in O(1).
3026.pitfall: Keeping the earliest prefix for a value rather than the smallest.

3169.title: Count Days Without Meetings
3169.idea: Sort and merge the meetings, then subtract merged lengths from the total days.
3169.pitfall: Off by one, since a meeting from s to e covers e - s + 1 days.

3355.title: Zero Array Transformation I
3355.idea: Each query can lower any index it covers by at most 1, so a difference array gives each index's coverage, and the target is reachable when coverage >= nums[i] everywhere.
3355.pitfall: Placing the closing decrement at r instead of r + 1, which shortens every range by one.

3356.title: Zero Array Transformation II
3356.idea: Using more queries never hurts, so binary search the prefix length k and test it with a difference array of total decrement per index.
3356.pitfall: Forgetting the k = 0 case, where the input is already all zero.
3356.time: O((n + q) log q), q = queries

3453.title: Separate Squares I
3453.idea: Area below a horizontal line grows with its height, so binary search y over reals for where the area below reaches half the total.
3453.pitfall: Stopping at any balanced y, when the area can stay flat across a gap and the lowest such y is required.
3453.time: O(n log(R / e)), R = y range, e = precision

3532.title: Path Existence Queries in a Graph I
3532.idea: In a sorted array any edge implies every adjacent gap between its ends is within maxDiff, so components are the maximal runs split at gaps above maxDiff.
3532.pitfall: Building the pair graph, which can have O(n^2) edges.

3592.title: Inverse Coin Change
3592.idea: Go through amounts in increasing order with a ways table from coins found so far, and if the table is one short at i, then i must be a coin, so add it with an unbounded knapsack update.
3592.pitfall: Accepting any mismatch, when a gap other than 0 or 1 means no coin set exists.

3623.title: Count Number of Trapezoids I
3623.idea: Group points by y, so a row with c points has C(c, 2) horizontal segments, and the answer sums products over all row pairs using a running total of earlier rows.
3623.pitfall: Looping over all row pairs, which is quadratic when one pass with a running sum suffices.

3625.title: Count Number of Trapezoids II
3625.idea: Count pairs of parallel segments on different lines by grouping all point pairs by slope and line, then subtract parallelograms once, found as segment pairs with a shared midpoint and different slopes.
3625.pitfall: Forgetting that a parallelogram has two parallel pairs, so it gets counted twice.
